cases.evidence_note: Stage 16, predicted by hand from the archived i1040gi (IRA Deduction Worksheet, Social Security Benefits Worksheet, Tax Table), p590a, f8606, i8606 and f8880, by two independent agents that did not see the encoding; recorded after comparison. Facts: Married filing jointly, both aged 39. You are covered by a plan at work; wages $66,000. Your spouse is not covered; wages $51,500. Taxable interest $9,000. Each of you contributes $7,000 to a traditional IRA. The two predictors differed here only on rounding: Pub. 590-A Example 1 prints $6,825, but its own Worksheet 1-2 line 4 ("If the result isn't a multiple of $10, round it to the next highest multiple of $10") and the i1040gi IRA Deduction Worksheet line 7 ("increase it to the next multiple of $10") give $6,830; the expected values follow the printed rule (predictor B), and the example's figure is an open owner question. Working (predictor B): 1040 line 9 = 66,000+51,500+9,000 = 126,500. WS (i1040gi p.97): 2a 146,000 (covered, MFJ); 2b 246,000 (not covered). 3 = 126,500; 4 = 0; 5 = 126,500 both. 6a = 19,500 (<20,000, covered column -> line 7); 6b = 119,500 (>=10,000, uncovered column -> 7b = 7,000). 7a = 19,500 x 0.35 = 6,825 -> next multiple of $10 = 6,830 (p.98 line 7). 8 = 117,500 wages; 9 = 0; 10 = 117,500. 11a = 11b = 7,000. 12a = min(6,830,117,500,7,000) = 6,830; 12b = 7,000. s1 line 20 = 13,830 = line 26. Form 8606 (you): line 1 = 7,000 - 6,830 = 170; line 2 = 0; line 3 = 170; no distribution/conversion -> line 14 = 170. AGI = 126,500 - 13,830 = 112,670. Std ded MFJ 31,500. Line 15 = 81,170. Tax Table MFJ 81,150-81,200 = 9,264. Line 17 = 0 so line 18 = 9,264. Saver's credit: AGI > 79,000, not available.

No traditional IRA contribution. No excess contribution, no recharacterization, no IRA distribution. Two agents worked the return by hand from the archived text without the encoding and agreed on every asserted value; the expected values are theirs.

ira.line9.remedy: Self-employment income counts as IRA compensation only where your personal services are a material income-producing factor; Schedule C income mainly from investments or property is outside this tool.

cite.locator: pp. 6–7, Self-employment income, "earnings from your trade or business (provided your personal services are a material income-producing factor)"

cases.evidence_note: Inputs are stage16.ira.i5 with wages of $85,000: a single filer age 50 or older, covered by a plan at work, contributing $8,000. Line 2 is $89,000 and line 5 (modified AGI) $85,000, so line 6 is $4,000; the column takes 80% for a person age 50 or older ($3,200), already a multiple of $10 and at least $200, so line 7 is $3,200, and the deduction is the smallest of line 7, line 10 (compensation) and line 11 (the $8,000 contributed): $3,200 on Schedule 1 line 20. Predicted from i1040gi pp. 97-98 (IRA Deduction Worksheet, lines 2, 6 and 7, 'Multiply line 6 by 70% (0.70) (or by 80% (0.80) in the column for the IRA of a person who is age 50 or older at the end of 2025)'); no independent human hand-work is claimed.

Inputs are stage16.ira.i8 with the taxpayer age 50 or older contributing $8,000: a joint return, both spouses covered by a plan at work, wages $70,000 and $60,000. Line 2 is $146,000 in both columns and line 5 (modified AGI) $130,000, so line 6 is $16,000 in both; the taxpayer's column takes 40% ($6,400) and the spouse's 35% ($5,600), both multiples of $10 and at least $200, so lines 7a and 7b are $6,400 and $5,600; the deductions are the smallest of line 7, compensation and the contributions ($8,000 and $7,000): $6,400 and $5,600, $12,000 on Schedule 1 line 20. Predicted from i1040gi pp. 97-98 (IRA Deduction Worksheet, line 7, 'Multiply line 6 by 35% (0.35) (or by 40% (0.40) in the column for the IRA of a person who is age 50 or older at the end of 2025)'); no independent human hand-work is claimed.

Stage 16 return I3 (single, aged 40, covered by a plan at work, traditional IRA contribution $7,000) with wages $78,999.50; the return is figured in dollars and cents. IRA Deduction Worksheet (i1040gi p. 97): line 2 $89,000; line 3 $78,999.50; line 4 $0; line 5 $78,999.50; line 6 = $89,000 - $78,999.50 = $10,000.50. "If single ... and the result is $10,000 or more, enter the applicable amount below on line 7 ... $7,000 if under age 50": line 7 $7,000 (not 70% of line 6, $7,000.35 rounded up to $7,010). Line 8 and 10 $78,999.50; line 11 $7,000; line 12 the smallest of 7, 10, 11 = $7,000; Schedule 1 line 20 $7,000.
